𝐉𝐀𝐌Ó𝐍 𝐉𝐀𝐌Ó𝐍, 𝟏𝟗𝟗𝟐.⁣
⁣
This one is controversial to say the least. 𝐉𝐚𝐦ó𝐧, 𝐉𝐚𝐦ó𝐧 (𝟏𝟗𝟗𝟐) is a dark and sarcastic romance that can look completely ridiculous if taken at face value. But beneath the sex, food, pigs, trucks and naked bullfighting, director Bigas Luna uses the story to take aim at Spanish culture, particularly machismo, sexual hypocrisy, class and traditional ideas of masculinity. It’s not quite a comedy, but rather a strange and provocative satire whose cultural references perhaps explain why some of its most passionate fans (and critics) have been Spanish.⁣
⁣
At the center of all this movie are three young actors who would go on to have major careers: Penélope Cruz, Javier Bardem and Jordi Mollà. Cruz was only 18 during filming, while Bardem was 22. Their chemistry gives the movie much of its energy, but the experience had a complicated effect on Cruz. 𝐉𝐚𝐦ó𝐧, 𝐣𝐚𝐦ó𝐧 (𝟏𝟗𝟗𝟐) turned her into a sex symbol almost overnight and Cruz struggled with the attention. She later explained that she developed a strong rejection of anything sexual or sensual, cut her hair very short and avoided love scenes or even kissing scenes for years. She also remembered crying on the final day of filming, terrified that the movie might end her career rather than begin it.⁣
⁣
Instead, 𝐉𝐚𝐦ó𝐧 𝐉𝐚𝐦ó𝐧 (𝟏𝟗𝟗𝟐) helped launch her career. And it also introduced her to the man she would eventually marry. Despite their intense chemistry on screen, Cruz and Bardem did not become a couple during the film. Their lives went in different directions, and more than 15 years passed before they worked closely together again in Vicky Cristina Barcelona (2008). This time, the chemistry became real. Bardem later revealed that neither dared make the first move during filming. It was only at the wrap party that something finally happened. They married privately in 2010 and later had two children.⁣

source_details.title: Jamón jamón
source_details.synopsis: Jamón jamón (Spanish pronunciation: [xaˈmoŋ xaˈmon]; English: Ham, Ham) is a 1992 Spanish romantic tragicomedy film directed by Bigas Luna and starring Javier Bardem, Jordi Mollà, and Penélope Cruz in her debut film. It centers on a young woman named Silvia who becomes pregnant by Jose Luis, the scion of a small but powerful underwear manufacturing empire, and the disastrous fallout of their relationship. The movie engages in word play and puns, and rhapsodises on the juxtaposition of old and new in Spain, as well as many other emotional contrasts such as erotic desire and food.
